title: Newton's Laws of Motion
definitions: An object at rest stays at rest, and an object in motion stays in motion with the same speed and direction unless acted upon by an unbalanced force
Force equals mass times acceleration (F = ma)
For every action, there is an equal and opposite reaction
The resistance of an object to a change in its state of motion
The sum of all forces acting on an object

title: Electricity and Magnetism
definitions: The current through a conductor is directly proportional to the voltage and inversely proportional to the resistance (V = IR)
The difference in electric potential between two points
The flow of electric charge
The opposition to the flow of electric current
A region where an electric charge experiences a force

title: Waves and Optics
definitions: The distance between consecutive corresponding points of a wave
The number of wave cycles passing a point per unit time
The maximum displacement of a wave from its equilibrium position
The change in frequency of a wave in relation to an observer moving relative to the wave source
The superposition of two or more waves resulting in a new wave pattern

title: Modern Physics
definitions: Einstein's theory that describes the relationship between space, time, and gravity
The branch of physics that deals with the behavior of matter and energy at the atomic and subatomic levels
The emission of electrons when light shines on a material
The principle that states that the position and momentum of a particle cannot be simultaneously measured with arbitrary precision
The concept that all particles exhibit both wave-like and particle-like properties

title: Thermodynamics
definitions: Energy cannot be created or destroyed, only transformed
The entropy of an isolated system always increases
A measure of the disorder or randomness of a system
The transfer of energy due to a temperature difference
The transfer of energy due to a force acting through a distance

title: Fundamental Forces and Particles
definitions: The force of attraction between all objects with mass
The force between electrically charged particles
The force that holds protons and neutrons together in the nucleus
The force responsible for radioactive decay
A particle that gives mass to other particles

title: Fluid Mechanics
definitions: Force per unit area
As the speed of a fluid increases, the pressure decreases
The buoyant force on an object equals the weight of the fluid displaced by the object
Pressure applied to a fluid is transmitted equally in all directions
A measure of a fluid's resistance to flow
